title: Traumatic disseminated intravascular coagulation: a narrative review of modern concepts in pathophysiology, diagnosis, and management
one_line_summary: This review delineates traumatic DIC as a dynamic immunothrombotic spectrum evolving from early hyperfibrinolysis to late microvascular thrombosis, emphasizing early goal-directed resuscitation and phase-specific targeted therapies.
key_pearls: Traumatic DIC is an evolving spectrum that transitions from an early **hyperfibrinolytic phenotype** (driven by endothelial **t-PA** release) to a late **thrombotic phenotype** (driven by **PAI-1** surge and persistent **thrombin generation**).
Early **tranexamic acid (TXA)** administration within **3 hours** of injury is **critical**; **survival** benefit decreases by **10%** for every **15-minute** delay in administration.

Acquired **antithrombin (AT)** depletion in acute trauma occurs primarily via physical **extravasation/leakage** across damaged endothelium rather than pure consumption; admission **AT activity < 80%** independently predicts DIC and **mortality**.
Goal-directed resuscitation guided by viscoelastic testing (**TEG/ROTEM**) reduces early hemorrhagic **mortality** (**19.6%** vs **36.4%**) and minimizes unnecessary plasma and platelet utilization.

European guidelines recommend a **fibrinogen-first** strategy using **fibrinogen concentrate** or cryoprecipitate when plasma fibrinogen falls **≤ 1.5 g/L**, avoiding fresh frozen plasma for isolated hypofibrinogenemia.

Empiric administration of **4-factor PCC** in trauma resuscitation is discouraged, as it fails to reduce blood transfusion requirements and **significantly** increases **thromboembolic events** (**PROCOAG** trial).

sections.heading: Introduction and Modern Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
- **Traumatic DIC** represents an uncontrolled, systemic thromboinflammatory failure originating from **trauma-induced coagulopathy (TIC)**.
- The **2020 ISTH consensus** unified TIC and traumatic DIC into a single dynamic spectrum, defining TIC as the early stage that can progress to overt DIC.
- Modern pathophysiological models conceptualize traumatic DIC as a breakdown of physiological **immunothrombosis**.
- Nationwide Japanese registry data show that while sepsis-associated DIC **mortality** has **significantly** declined, traumatic DIC **mortality** has shown **no clinically meaningful change** over the last decade.
section_pearls: TIC and traumatic DIC represent a continuous spectrum rather than distinct entities.
Traumatic DIC mortality rates have stagnated over the past decade despite advances in sepsis DIC care.

sections.heading: Pathophysiology: Damage-Associated Molecular Patterns and Immunothrombosis
sections.content:
- Massive cell injury releases **damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs)**—including **histones**, **mitochondrial DNA**, and **HMGB1**—into circulation within **< 30 minutes**.
- DAMPs stimulate myeloid cell inflammasomes, triggering pyroptosis and releasing **tissue factor (TF)**-bearing extracellular vesicles that directly initiate coagulation.
- **Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs)** form a prothrombotic scaffold, entrap and activate platelets, and release **neutrophil elastase** to cleave natural anticoagulants.
- Extracellular **histones** assemble an alternative prothrombinase complex, driving an accelerated **thrombin burst**.
section_pearls: Circulating histones and DAMPs trigger direct extrinsic coagulation and endothelial destruction within 30 minutes post-injury.

sections.heading: Dynamic Phenotypic Shift: Hyperfibrinolysis to Microvascular Thrombosis
sections.content:
- The acute phase features a **hyperfibrinolytic phenotype** caused by rapid **t-PA** release from endothelial granules, exceeding initial **PAI-1** levels.
- Transition to the **thrombotic phenotype** occurs over hours due to transcriptional upregulation of **PAI-1** from platelets and stressed endothelium.
- **Thrombin generation** is triggered immediately post-injury and persists continuously through both fibrinolytic and thrombotic phases.
- Dense, small-fibered clots produced by excessive thrombin generation resist lysis, driving microvascular thrombosis and **MODS**.
- **Platelet-derived extracellular vesicles (PEVs)** act as prohemostatic agents early but promote **deep vein thrombosis (DVT)** in later stages.
section_pearls: Thrombin generation remains continuously elevated across both early hyperfibrinolytic and late thrombotic phases.
PEVs exhibit a dual functional role: early hemostatic enhancement versus late prothrombotic DVT risk.

sections.heading: Traumatic Brain Injury-Induced Coagulopathy (TBI-IC)
sections.content:
- **TBI-IC** is driven by blood-brain barrier disruption releasing **brain-derived extracellular vesicles (BDEVs)** rich in **tissue factor (TF)** and phosphatidylserine.
- Unlike classic shock-driven TIC, **TBI-IC** initiation occurs independently of systemic hypoperfusion or serum **lactate** levels.
- TBI-IC rapidly progresses from localized consumptive hypercoagulation to systemic **DIC with hyperfibrinolysis**.
- Admission coagulopathy (**PT-INR**, **D-dimer**) in TBI patients strongly correlates with **progressive hemorrhagic injury**.
section_pearls: TBI-IC is triggered by brain-derived microvesicles carrying tissue factor, independent of systemic hypoperfusion.

sections.heading: Endotheliopathy and Anticoagulant Breakdown
sections.content:
- Coagulopathy is driven by a two-hit model: **shock-induced endotheliopathy (SHINE)** via catecholamine surge, followed by **resuscitation-associated endotheliopathy (RAsE)** from crystalloid dilutional stress.
- Shedding of **syndecan-1** strips the **endothelial glycocalyx (EGL)** of heparan sulfates, destroying the local **antithrombin (AT)** binding environment.
- Acute drops in circulating AT activity are primarily caused by vascular **leakage/extravasation** into interstitial spaces (**AT** levels strongly correlate with albumin, *r* = **0.702**).
- Severe **AT activity < 80%** on admission independently predicts traumatic DIC development and **mortality**.
- Degradation of the EGL produces an imbalance between **VWF** multimers and **ADAMTS13**, accelerating microthrombosis.
section_pearls: Antithrombin depletion in early trauma is predominantly caused by transvascular leakage rather than consumption.
Admission AT activity < 80% is an independent predictor of DIC and overall mortality.

sections.heading: Diagnostic Scoring Systems and Viscoelastic Assays
sections.content:
- The **JAAM DIC score** demonstrates **superior** sensitivity for early traumatic DIC compared to the **ISTH overt DIC score**.
- Laboratory predictors of DIC include admission **lactate ≥ 4.8 mmol/L** and **PT-INR ≥ 1.2**.
- Goal-directed resuscitation guided by **viscoelastic testing (VET)** reduces 28-day **mortality** compared to standard assays (**19.6%** vs **36.4%**).
- Provocative assays like **tPA-TEG** and **plasmin-TEG** rapidly unmask fibrinolytic inhibitor depletion and predict massive transfusion needs in **< 3 minutes**.
section_pearls: VET-guided hemostatic resuscitation significantly improves survival compared to conventional coagulation testing.
Provocative tPA/plasmin-TEG assays identify latent fibrinolysis derangements within 3 minutes.

sections.heading: Phase-Specific Management: Resuscitation and Anticoagulation
sections.content:
- **Early Phase**: Prioritizes surgical/endovascular bleeding control, prehospital **tranexamic acid (TXA)** within **3 hours**, and hemostatic resuscitation.
- **Resuscitation Ratios**: The **PROPPR** trial demonstrated that a 1:1:1 ratio reduces exsanguination death, with Bayesian analysis showing a **99.0%** probability of **3-hour** **survival** benefit.
- **Fibrinogen Repletion**: European guidelines advocate FC or cryoprecipitate when fibrinogen falls **≤ 1.5 g/L**; FFP alone failed to correct coagulopathy in **52%** of patients in the **RETIC** trial.
- **PCC Avoidance**: Empiric 4-factor PCC increases thromboembolic events without reducing transfusion volume (**PROCOAG** trial).
- **Late Phase**: Focuses on **VTE prophylaxis** with **LMWH**. **Antithrombin supplementation** restores enoxaparin responsiveness in patients exhibiting **heparin resistance**.
section_pearls: Target fibrinogen replacement when levels are ≤ 1.5 g/L using concentrate or cryoprecipitate rather than plasma.
Avoid empiric 4-factor PCC in trauma resuscitation due to proven thromboembolic risks.

sections.heading: Prognostic Indicators in Traumatic DIC
sections.content:
- High admission **JAAM DIC score**, **lactate ≥ 4.8 mmol/L**, and **AT activity < 80%** independently predict **MODS** and **mortality**.
- Persistent elevation of circulating **histones** over the first **6 hours** post-injury indicates high risk of **mortality**.
- Longitudinal **D-dimer** trajectory patterns ("high-gradual decline") provide **superior** prognostic accuracy over single static measurements.
section_pearls: Failure to clear circulating histones within 6 hours post-injury portends a fatal outcome.

strengths_limitations:
- **Strengths**: Comprehensive synthesis of recent immunothrombotic pathophysiology, direct comparisons of diagnostic scoring systems, clear phased clinical management guidelines, and inclusion of recent clinical trials.
- **Limitations**: Narrative review methodology without systematic protocol; ongoing international disagreement regarding late-phase targeted anticoagulants (**AT** and **rhTM**).

drugs_doses.dose: 1 g IV loading dose over 10 minutes, followed by 1 g IV over 8 hours; administered within 3 hours of injury
drugs_doses.indication: Early hyperfibrinolytic phenotype in traumatic DIC and severe trauma hemorrhage
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Loss of efficacy and potential increased mortality if delayed > 3 hours post-injury

drugs_doses.dose: Targeted dosing (typically 2-4 g IV) to maintain plasma fibrinogen > 1.5 g/L
drugs_doses.indication: Hypofibrinogenemia and reduced clot firmness in trauma-induced coagulopathy

drugs_doses.dose: Weight- and INR-based dosing per local transfusion protocols
drugs_doses.indication: Targeted factor replacement in severe trauma hemorrhage
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Increased risk of thromboembolic events; thrombin overshoot

drugs_doses.dose: Dosed to restore AT activity > 80% (ex vivo / targeted clinical protocol)
drugs_doses.indication: Heparin resistance during VTE prophylaxis or late-phase thrombotic DIC with severe AT deficiency
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Increased bleeding risk when combined with systemic anticoagulants; unproven international mortality benefit

drugs_doses.dose: Standard IV weight-based infusion per DIC protocol
drugs_doses.indication: Late thrombotic phase of DIC / microvascular thrombosis management
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Bleeding complications; unproven mortality benefit in global trauma guidelines

drugs_doses.dose: Standard prophylactic dosing (e.g., enoxaparin 30 mg SC BID or 40 mg SC daily)
drugs_doses.indication: Venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in the late hypercoagulable phase of trauma
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Bleeding risk; ineffective response (heparin resistance) if baseline AT activity is < 80%
